names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 mai, «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Irina».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Μαΐου, «Αγία Ειρήνη η Μεγαλομάρτυς», with the rank words left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 5. мај ст. ст., „Света великомученица Ирина.“ Света is no rank; великомученица is the `great-martyr` this folder already carries in `types` and `honorific.js` composes back, so stripping it leaves the bare forename and nothing else. **Magedon, which the English display name keeps, is in the body and not in the heading** — „у некоме граду Магедону“ — so it is not part of the form, and no epithet was invented to hold the folder out of the fold with `irene-of-aquileia`'s equally bare Ирина.

Read out of the calendar’s name link for 5 мая ст. ст., which gives «Святая великомученица Ирина»; the rank words are not part of the stored form, and the calendar gives her no epithet beside the bare name on this day. The baptismal change of name the lives give — «до крещения носила имя Пенелопа» — is in the life and is not a second stored form.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 мая ст. ст. — «Вмц. Ирины (I-II).»

attestations.note: The calendar gives her three life pages and they do not agree about where she came from. life6650 makes her «родом славянка», a Slav by birth, and her father Ликиний the ruler of «города Магеддона в Македонии» — the Magedon this folder's display name keeps her under; life4837 makes him ruler of «области Мигдония в Македонии», a province; life997 of «города Мигдонии (Македония, или Фракия)», and hedges the country. All three keep the same father, the same baptism at the hands of the apostle Тимофей, the same three birds, the same Седекия and the same cave at Ephesus, so they are three tellings of one dossier and not two women. Nothing was moved and the display name was not changed. `dates` gained a `floruit` the folder had none of. The stored Russian form is the bare «Ирина», which is all the calendar's name link gives; the fold «ирина» ALREADY HELD two folders before this batch, on the Serbian form both of them store, and it is unread. This batch DOES NOT WIDEN IT — irene-of-magedon is already one of the two — and so writes no key for it. Read 8 October 2026.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 mai — «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Irina»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Μαΐου — «Αγία Ειρήνη η Μεγαλομάρτυς»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps her, and it is plainly the same woman: daughter of Licinius and Licinia, from the city of Magedon, first named Penelope, shut in a tower at six under an elder Apellianos who wrote the acts of her contest, the dove and the eagle and the raven, the horse that killed her father and her raising him, the brazen oxen, the death and rising at Mesembria, the end at Ephesus and the empty coffin. **No `dates` object is added, and this is the reason:** saint.gr states «Η Αγία Μεγαλομάρτυς Ειρήνη άθλησε κατά τον 4ο αιώνα μ.Χ.» and «μέχρι την ημέρα της κοιμήσεως αυτής, το 315 μ.Χ.», while the folder's own life carries doxologia's argued note that her Licinius was a kinglet of Magedon and not the emperor, and that she therefore belongs to the first century, near the days of the apostles, the priest Timothy who baptised her having had his priesthood from the Apostle Paul. Two sources three centuries apart is not an interval worth recording, and neither year is weakened by the other here; the disagreement is written into the life instead. **What the Greek does add and the folder lacked**: the Persian kings Σεδεκίας and Σαπώριος Α΄ under whom she suffered, Kallipolis of the Hellespont under Noumerianos as the place of the brazen oxen, Ephesus as the place of her repose, the relics — «Απότμημα του Ιερού Λειψάνου της Αγίας βρίσκεται στη Μονή Κύκκου Κύπρου και στον Ιερό Ναό του Αγίου Γεωργίου των Ελλήνων Βενετίας» — and the hymns, of which the folder had none in Greek. **The page prints three apolytikia, two kontakia, a megalynarion, an oikos and four kathismata; only the first apolytikion and the first kontakion are stored, both of them proper and both naming her.** Its closing note reports two variant traditions against its own account — the western martyrologies making her suffer at Thessalonica by fire, the Menologion of Basil II making her beheaded — which is the page weighing witnesses, not doubting itself: her entry carries no asterisk.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.05.2026 (5. мај ст. ст.) — „Света великомученица Ирина.“

attestations.note: **The day is Julian 5 May, the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek keep her on**, and this is the third full account of her read for this folder. No existing row was moved. The identification is the whole story: a father named Licinius who was a king at Magedon, the pagan name Penelope, the teacher Apelian, the priest Timothy of the Apostle Paul who baptised her, the king Sedekiah and his son Savah, the three heated brazen oxen, Mesembria, and the grave found empty on the fourth day with Apelian standing by it. **No year was taken.** This page says only „Живела у времена апостолска“, which has no bounds; the folder holds no `dates` because the Romanian page argues the first century and saint.gr gives the fourth and 315, and this book **siding with the earlier reading does not make it a bound**. New to the corpus from this page: that **some think she was a Slav** — „Неки мисле да је била Словенкиња“, which no other account of her carries; that **Apelian taught her the Christian faith**, where the Romanian page has him only read the birds; that Timothy was the **disciple** of the Apostle Paul and brought her his letters to read; that Sedekiah's ditch held **scorpions as well as snakes** and that she was buried in it **up to the head**; that the saw rebounded from her **as from stone**; that Savah **shod her with nails, loaded a sack of sand on her and bridled her** and had her driven like a beast out of the city, where she said „Заиста сам као скот пред Тобом, Господе!“, and that **the earth opened and swallowed her tormentors**; that the eparch **Ваводин** took her to **град Константину**, a place neither other account names, where the Romanian page has his grating at Callinicum; and that she brought **more than a hundred thousand** pagans to the faith. **One deliberate fold**: the heading's bare Ирина is already held by `irene-of-aquileia`, and the row is in this batch's commit message. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Irina, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc, și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfintei Mari Mucenițe Irina», Glasul 4

english.text: Thy ewe-lamb, O Jesus, Irene, cries out with a great voice: Thee, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking Thee I am in torment; I am crucified with Thee and buried with Thee in Thy baptism; I suffer for Thee that I may reign in Thee, and I die for Thee that I may live for Thee. Receive me as a sacrifice without spot, who offer myself to Thee in love. At her prayers, in Thy mercy, save our souls.

hymns.text: Εἰρήνης τὸν ἄρχοντα, ἰχνηλατοῦσα σεμνή, εἰρήνης ἐπώνυμος, δι' ἐπιπνοίας Θεοῦ, ἐδείχθης πανεύφημε, σὺ γὰρ τοῦ πολέμου, τᾶς ἐνέδρας φυγοῦσα, ἤθλησας ὑπὲρ φύσιν, ὡς παρθένος φρονίμη, διὸ Μεγαλομάρτυς Εἰρήνη, εἰρήνην ἠμὶν αἴτησαι.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε, the first of three on the page of «Αγία Ειρήνη η Μεγαλομάρτυς»

english.text: Tracking out the Prince of peace, O modest one, thou wast shown by the inspiration of God to bear the name of peace, O all-praised; for having fled the ambushes of the war, thou didst contend beyond nature as a prudent virgin. Wherefore, O great martyr Irene, ask peace for us.

hymns.text: Τὴν καλλιπάρθενον ὑμνήσωμεν πάντες, νύμφην Χριστοῦ, ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν ἀναστάσαν, ἧν ὁ Θεός ἐδόξασε σημείοις φρικτοῖς, Εἴλκυσε γὰρ πλῆθος ἄπειρον, ἀσεβῶν ἐν τῇ πίστει, καὶ θεόθεν ἔλαβε, τὴν Χριστώνυμον κλήσιν, ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ γὰρ Ἄγγελος ἐλθών, ἐκ Πηνελόπης Εἰρήνην ἐκάλεσε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ὁ ὑψωθεῖς, the first of two on the page of «Αγία Ειρήνη η Μεγαλομάρτυς»

english.text: Let us all hymn the fair virgin, the bride of Christ, risen from the dead, whom God glorified with fearful signs; for she drew a countless multitude of the ungodly into the faith, and received from God her calling by Christ's name, since an angel of God came and from Penelope named her Irene.

hymns.text: Агница Твоя, Иисусе, Ирина/ зовет велиим гласом:/ Тебе, Женише мой, люблю,/ и, Тебе ищущи, страдальчествую,/ и сраспинаюся, и спогребаюся Крещению Твоему,/ и стражду Тебе ради,/ яко да царствую в Тебе, и умираю за Тя,/ да и живу с Тобою,/ но яко жертву непорочную приими мя,/ с любовию пожершуюся Тебе.// Тоя молитвами, яко Милостив, спаси души наша.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 мая ст. ст., «Тропарь мученицы Ирины», глас 4 — the common of a woman martyr, with her name set into it, as the same calendar sets other names into the same text

english.text: Thy ewe-lamb Irene cries out to thee with a great voice, O Jesus: thee, my Bridegroom, I love; seeking thee I contend, and I am crucified and buried with thee in thy baptism; I suffer for thy sake, that I may reign in thee, and I die for thee that I may live with thee. Receive me as a spotless sacrifice, offered to thee in love. By her prayers, as thou art merciful, save our souls.

hymns.text: Девства добротами преиспещренна, дево,/ страдальчеством была еси краснейшая, Ирино,/ кровьми твоими истекшими обагрена,/ прелесть же низложившая безбожия.// Сего ради и прияла еси почести победы рукою Создателя твоего.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 5 мая ст. ст., «Кондак мученицы Ирины», глас 4

english.text: Adorned with the beauties of virginity, O maiden, thou wast made fairer still by thy martyrdom, Irene, reddened by thine own blood poured out, and thou didst throw down the deceit of godlessness. Therefore hast thou received the honours of victory from the hand of thy Creator.

floruit.note: days.pravoslavie.ru gives her three lives and all three put her in the first century: life4837 and life997 open «жила в I веке», and life6650 «жила во второй половине I века». The day line closes her «(I-II)», the first or the second century, which is wider than any of the lives and is recorded here rather than in the interval. No source read gives a year for her birth or her death, and the lives end with her body not found in the cave, so there is neither a birth nor a death object.
